# Problem 1
In this session, we created beeswarm-style boxplot to display our T-cell frequencies on the y-axis, and timepoint on the x-axis. Using the concepts covered this week, swap out “timepoint” for the “Condition” variable. Adjust other layer arguments accordingly until you can return a similar plot at the end of the class. Finally, figure out how to switch around the order the Condition values are displayed on the x-axis.

```{r}
# Load packages
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggcyto)
library(CytoML)
library(ggbeeswarm)

# Load dataset
Folder <- file.path("data")
CSVFile <- list.files(Folder, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)
Data <- read.csv(CSVFile, check.names = FALSE)

# Amend columns
Data <- Data |> 
    mutate(TcellProportion=Tcells_count/CD45_count) |>
    mutate(TcellFrequency=TcellProportion *100) |>
    mutate(TcellFrequency=round(TcellFrequency, 1))
Data$timepoint <- factor(Data$timepoint)

# Plot formatting vectors
shape_sex <- c("Female" = 22, "Male" = 21)
fill_sex <- c("Female" = "white", "Male" = "black")

# Plot T-cell frequencies vs. Condition
ggplot(Data) + aes(x= Condition, y=TcellFrequency) +
     geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgrey") + geom_beeswarm(size=2.5, cex=2.5, aes(shape=infant_sex, fill=infant_sex)) +
     scale_shape_manual(values=shape_sex) + scale_fill_manual(values=fill_sex) + theme_bw()

# Change condition order on plot

# 1. Change condition from character vector to factor
Data$Condition <- factor(Data$Condition)
str(Data$Condition)

# 2. Use levels = to change the order of the factors
levels(Data$Condition)

Data$Condition <- factor(Data$Condition, levels = c("PPD", "SEB", "Ctrl"))
levels(Data$Condition)

# 3. Plot updated graph
ggplot(Data) + aes(x= Condition, y=TcellFrequency) +
     geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgrey") + geom_beeswarm(size=2.5, cex=2.5, aes(shape=infant_sex, fill=infant_sex)) +
     scale_shape_manual(values=shape_sex) + scale_fill_manual(values=fill_sex) + theme_bw()
```

# Problem 2
Circle back to the CytoML-ggcyto flowplot, and modify it until happy with the visual appearance. You may use any resource on the internet to assist, but you must document your steps so that we can also repeat them.

```{r}
# Load FlowJo wsp file
FlowJoWsp <- list.files(path = Folder, pattern = ".wsp", full = TRUE)
ws <- open_flowjo_xml(FlowJoWsp)
gs <- flowjo_to_gatingset(ws=ws, name=1, path = Folder, additional.keys = "GROUPNAME")

# Original plot
Plot <- ggcyto(gs[6], subset="Tcells", aes(x="CD8", y="CD4")) + geom_hex(bins=80) + theme

# Fix sample names
sampleNames(gs)
pd <- pData(gs)
pd$sample_id <- sampleNames(gs)
pData(gs) <- pd

# Updated plot
Plot <- ggcyto(gs[6], subset="Tcells", aes(x="CD8", y="CD4")) + geom_hex(bins=80) + labs(x = "CD8 BV650", y = "CD4 BUV805", title = "T Cell Populations") + facet_wrap(~sample_id) + theme_bw() + theme(
     # change facet strip text
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14, colour = "red", face = "bold"),
    # change strip box colour
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"), 
    # change background grid sizing and colour
    panel.grid = element_line(linewidth = 0.1, colour = "grey"),
    #change plot title and axis text
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    # Change axis text
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12, colour = "blue")
  )
Plot
```

# Problem 3
In Mismatched Assumptions, we saw two examples of a histogram/density overlay showing the distribution of a variable on the x-axis. Similar to what we did during class to show values according to a different data column, try to modify the plot to show data on the basis of group (whether condition, ptype, infant_sex, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(Data) + aes(x=Condition) + geom_histogram() 
ggplot(Data) + aes(x=ptype) + geom_density() 

str(Data$Condition)
str(Data$ptype)
```

When copying the histrogram/ density plots from the walkthrough and changing the x-axis to the suggested group columns, an error occurs as a continuous x aesthetic is required but the group data is categorical (factor/ character). geom_bar() can be used for categorical variables instead:

```{r}
ggplot(Data) + aes(x=Condition) + geom_bar() 
ggplot(Data) + aes(x=ptype) + geom_bar() 
ggplot(Data) + aes(x=infant_sex) + geom_bar() 
```
